relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence: To access an HTTP server using cURL, the Eventing Function needs to declare a URL binding and pass the alias of the binding to curl() calls.

relations.subject: eventing:url-alias-binding
relations.object: URLs that are descendants of the URL specified in the binding
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; a better fit than the Capella twin's use of behavesDifferentlyUnder for this same fact, since it is a hard scoping restriction, not a variable behavior; object is a literal
relations.evidence: The binding specifies the remote URL to be accessed and all calls made using such a binding are limited to descendants of the URL specified in the binding.

relations.subject: eventing:url-alias-binding
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: The binding may also specify the authentication mechanism and credentials to use. Basic, Digest and Bearer authentication methods are supported.

relations.object: protocols other than http:// and https://

relations.subject: eventing:url-alias-binding
relations.evidence: HTTPS is used when the URL specifies the https:// prefix. Such a link uses https for encryption of contents, and if enabled, verifies the server certificate using the underlying OS support for server certificate verification. Client certificates are not currently supported.

relations.evidence: Users who wish to utilize custom encoding can do so by specifying an appropriate Content-Type using the _headers_ parameter of the request object and passing the custom encoded object as an ArrayBuffer as the _body_ parameter of the request.

relations.subject: eventing:url-alias-binding
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: Cookie support is turned off by default on a cURL binding. So, no cookies will be accepted from the remote server.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.object: persistent HTTP sessions/cookies across multiple curl() calls in different Function invocations
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: Note that Eventing utilizes multiple workers and multiple HTTP cURL sessions and so a Eventing Function cannot rely on all requests executing on the same HTTP session. It can rely on issued cookies being presented on subsequent requests only within the duration of a single Eventing Function invocation.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge and no RBAC role requirement appear anywhere on this page - curl() and its URL Alias Binding are documented purely as a language/networking specification, exactly as on the Capella twin.

cross_component_finding: The Capella twin independently minted an extraction-layer id, eventing:url-binding, for the exact construct this registry already promotes as eventing:url-alias-binding - a naming fork this record avoids repeating by reusing the promoted id directly, but flags for reconciliation since the twin's own extraction record still carries the unpromoted spelling. Separately, this page's Request/Response (un)marshalling tables - a closed, fully-specified type-mapping the Capella twin's extraction never captured as concepts at all - are exactly the kind of granular reference detail this batch keeps finding underrepresented in round 8's Capella extractions relative to the shared underlying content.
